weakest_scene.visible_evidence: At seg1:mid and seg1:end the projection scene stacks four text layers in the same 120px band: the kicker 'the data stops here', the title 'the world's growing e-waste pile', the annotation '62M (projected)  82M' printed straight across that title, and a duplicate mascot sitting on the title's first word. Below, the caption '2010. That's enough' / 'a half garbage' overlaps the big '82' readout, and the left and lower thirds of the frame are empty.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The projection machine draws its kicker, annotation and endpoint labels in absolute positions that assume no title block, so they land in the header band instead of near the line; the mascot is also placed twice (a header perch plus the stage instance) with no collision reservation for the title, and the line itself is scaled to a fraction of the frame leaving the rest void.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Lay seg1 out so nothing overlaps: reserve the header band for the title alone, anchor the '62M (projected)' / '82M' annotations beside their own points on the line (not in the header), drop the duplicate mascot so a single Data performs at the projection fan, and scale the measured/projected line to fill the frame so the empty left and lower thirds carry the shot.
